title: Launch Gardener's Journal: Signal Schedule & Sprint Notes (Apr 2027) - WIP
content:
Purpose
---
Notes and working plan for the upcoming phased rollout. This doc is intentionally conversational — think of it as the gardener's journal: daily observations, small interventions, and a schedule of signals we watch. The goal is a low-fuss, observable roll that preserves latency SLOs while letting feature flags mature across traffic slices.

Top-level goals
- Keep 99th percentile latency delta <= 10% vs baseline on production traffic during each phase.
- Ensure automatic fallback routes are tested and can be enacted in <5 minutes.
- Validate cost signals (GPU utilization, token cost per request) and stop if unit economics deviate >12%.

Quick summary of what’s changing
- Runtime: kernel selection update + KV cache tuning (optimize for long-context chat).
- Serving config: new batching policy (adaptive small-batch warmups) and an updated fallback model family (smaller quantized variant).
- Console: expose per-route token-cost sampling at 1% granularity.

Week-by-week signal schedule (high level)
Week 0 (preflight, days -10 to -4):
  - Smoke cluster provisioning, validate instance types and docker images. Owner: Liam.
  - Canary harness dry run in staging using synthetic traffic. Owner: Priya.
  - Telemetry sanity: ensure token-level tracing + cost metrics are flowing to observability. Owner: Diego.

Week 1 (micro-canary, days -3 to +1):
  - Route 0.5% traffic to canary pool (dedicated nodes). Watch: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, model divergence.
  - Cost gating: token-cost per 1000 requests sampled; abort if +15% vs baseline.
  - Manual check-in at 6 hours and 24 hours.

Week 2 (ramp, days +2 to +7):
  - 0.5% -> 5% traffic ramp across 48h windows. Observe heatmaps for seq-length distribution.
  - Enable KV prefix caching for 10% sample group. Evaluate hit rates and latency impact.
  - Run a small round of end-to-end QA flows (payments, auth, webhook delivery).

Week 3 (broadening, days +8 to +21):
  - 5% -> 35% over 7 days, with a hold and retro after hitting 20%.
  - Canary rollback rehearsals executed by on-call SRE (simulate silent failure and practice fallback).

Preflight checklist (must be green before any traffic shift)
- [ ] Artifacts: production image hashes verified and pinned. (Liam)
- [ ] Runbook: single-page rollback and contact tree published. (Maya)
- [ ] Dashboards: p50/p95/p99, error budget burn, token-cost per-route sampling at 1% enabled. (Observability)
- [ ] Chaos: simulated pod failure during staging ramp performed. (SRE)
- [ ] Security: KMS keys validated for private deploy paths, network policies smoke-tested. (Security)
- [ ] Compliance: audit log retention policy configured for this rollout. (Compliance)
- [ ] Feature flags: ability to pin model family per-tenant and per-route confirmed. (Product)

Signal definitions (what to watch, how to interpret)
- Latency p99: primary safety signal. If p99 > baseline * 1.10 for 5m sustained, pause ramp and investigate.
- Error rate: 5xx + model misgeneration signals > 0.2% sustained for 10m -> rollback candidate.
- Token cost delta: if cost/1000req > baseline * 1.12 for 30m -> alert Finance + SRE.
- Traffic skew: if top 5 clients > 40% of canary traffic, pause — need more representative mix.
- Behavioral regression: failing evals on the smoke prompt set (run daily) -> stop and triage with applied-ml.

Abort & rollback matrix (fast decisions)
- Severe latency spike: immediate traffic shift to fallback pool, create high-priority incident (page). Postmortem required within 48h.
- Correctness regressions: quick traffic reduction to previous pinned model for affected routes, preserve logs.
- Cost excess: throttle burst capacity and engage finance to evaluate temporary cap.

Operations runbook (short)
1) Small blast of 0.5% -> validate signals at 15, 60, 180 minutes.
2) If all green, continue ramp to next bucket over 48h.
3) At any alert threshold, enact automated policy: traffic re-route -> baked fallback model -> notify #release-ops channel.
4) If manual rollback chosen, use the gui + infra API (rollback tag v2027.03.21) and record reason in release notes.

Communication plan
- Day-of launch channel: #release-ops (mandatory check-ins), thread pinned by release lead.
- Customer-facing: coordinated note to Apps on the Dedicated plan if we exceed planned maintenance windows. Draft below.
- Post-release digest: 48h and 14-day followups with telemetry and cost analysis.

Draft release notes (internal -> to be trimmed for customer-facing)
Title: Kernel selection + KV cache tuning rollout (Apr 2027)
Summary: Small-scale rollout of runtime kernel selection updates and a KV cache configuration tuned for longer chat context. Expected outcomes are improved median latency for long-context requests and lower overall token spend for multi-turn sessions.
What changed:
- Runtime will prefer low-memory high-throughput kernels for large-sequence workloads when sequence estimate > 2048 tokens.
- KV cache TTL increased for session reuse, with adaptive eviction on memory pressure.
- Console: per-route sampling for token-cost is available at 1% and can be toggled in the observability tab.
Known limitations:
- Very short sessions (<32 tokens) may see slight latency regressions on p50 due to batching heuristics; flagged for optimizer follow-up.

Customer-facing blurb (short)
We’re rolling out an optimization to reduce inference cost and improve long-chat responsiveness. No action required. We'll monitor performance closely and notify customers if we adjust capacity.

Post-deploy checks (first 48 hours)
- Health: p50/p95/p99 back to baseline within 12 hours for all core routes.
- Cost: sampled token cost within planned variance.
- Regression tests: smoke-evals pass (daily).
- User incidents: triage any customer tickets within 4 hours.

Notes to self / open items
- Need a small script to auto-compare sampled token-cost pre/post; put on Priya's todo list.
- Add a synthetic test for very-short sessions to staging to reproduce p50 blip. (Diego)
- Confirm fallback model family has a quantized profile that matches accuracy gates. (Applied ML)
- Should we expose an automatic rollback window (e.g., if p99 spike > threshold twice in 24h)? Follow up with product on policy defaults.

Quick append: mini-checklist for on-call when alerted
- Acknowledge incident in pager within 2 minutes.
- Verify if signal is infrastructure vs model (check node cpu/gpu vs model logits divergence).
- If infra, re-route to alternate region and scale up safe pool. If model, revert to previous model tag.

Revision log
- 2027-03-25: Initial draft (Maya)
- 2027-03-28: Added ramp schedule and cost gate details (Liam)
- 2027-04-02: Updated abort matrix and added customer blurb (Priya)
- 2027-04-05: Minor wording changes and linked PR + Jira (Maya)

End of journal entry (for now)

---
Small note: this doc intentionally keeps some ambiguity — we want room for quick decisions during the runway. If anything in here blocks you from doing your job during the rollout, call it out and we'll make it explicit.
